questions.question: Q1. What is the fundamental mechanism behind shape change in a bilayer actuator?

answers.b: The differential expansion or contraction of two layers in response to a stimulus.
answers.c: Phase transformation from crystalline to amorphous state.
answers.d: Gravitational bending due to uneven mass distribution.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Actuation is driven by differential strain, not electrostatic forces.
explanations.b: Correct — Bending is induced when one layer expands or contracts more than the adjacent layer under a stimulus.
explanations.c: Incorrect — While phase changes can trigger strain, the bimetal mechanism itself relies on differential expansion.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Gravity has a negligible effect compared to internal stresses.

questions.question: Q2. Which historical equation forms the foundation for modeling curvature in bimetallic and bilayer 4D printed actuators?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Hooke's law relates stress and strain, but does not directly model bimetallic curvature.
explanations.b: Correct — Timoshenko's 1925 bimetal formula is the foundational equation relating layer properties and temperature changes to curvature.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Fick's First Law governs steady-state diffusion, not curvature dynamics.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The WLF equation characterizes temperature-dependent polymer relaxation, not bilayer bending.

questions.question: Q3. What does the term 'Swelling Anisotropy Ratio (As)' represent in wood or cellulose-based composite layers?

answers.a: The ratio of thermal expansion to moisture expansion.
answers.b: The ratio of transverse swelling strain to parallel swelling strain relative to the fiber direction.
answers.c: The ratio of active layer thickness to passive layer thickness.
answers.d: The ratio of wet density to dry density of the material.

explanations.a: Incorrect — It relates directional swelling strains, not thermal and moisture properties.
explanations.b: Correct — Swelling anisotropy (As) is the ratio of transverse swelling (perpendicular to fibers) to parallel swelling (parallel to fibers).
explanations.c: Incorrect — This describes the geometric thickness ratio (m).
explanations.d: Incorrect — Swelling anisotropy describes strain variation, not density ratios.

questions.question: Q4. According to Fick's Second Law, how does the characteristic diffusion time (tdiff) scale with the thickness (L) of an active hydrogel slab?

answers.c: Proportional to the square of thickness (tdiff ∝ L²).

explanations.a: Incorrect — Diffusion does not scale linearly with distance.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Increasing thickness increases diffusion time; it is not inversely proportional.
explanations.c: Correct — Fick's Second Law dictates that diffusion time scales with the square of the characteristic length (L²).
explanations.d: Incorrect — While the concentration profile has exponential-like curves, the characteristic time scales quadratically (L²).

questions.question: Q5. In 3D/4D printing via FDM, how does the deposition path (raster print angle) program the actuator's motion?

answers.a: It changes the chemical composition of the printed filament.
answers.b: It changes the local orientation of fibers or polymer chains, establishing directional expansion properties.
answers.c: It alters the glass transition temperature (Tg) of the polymer.
answers.d: It only affects the surface roughness of the printed part.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Printing orientation does not alter chemical composition.
explanations.b: Correct — The print path aligns polymer chains or embedded fibers, creating highly anisotropic expansion coefficients in specific directions.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Tg is an intrinsic material property and is not changed by the print path angle.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Print path angle determines the direction-dependent mechanical response, not just surface finish.

questions.question: Q6. In a bilayer actuator, what is 'Blocking Force (Fblock)'?

answers.a: The maximum force the actuator can exert to prevent it from dissolving in water.
answers.b: The force required to keep the actuator flat (prevent bending) under stimulus.
answers.c: The force that causes delamination between the two layers.
answers.d: The gravitational load of the actuator.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Has nothing to do with chemical dissolution.
explanations.b: Correct — Blocking force is the force required to completely constrain the actuator and prevent any out-of-plane deflection.
explanations.c: Incorrect — That is the interfacial shear/peeling force.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Blocking force is an active mechanical response, not static weight.

questions.question: Q7. What represents the total work output (W) of a bilayer actuator?

answers.a: The product of the mass and the acceleration of the actuator.
answers.b: The area under the force-deflection curve, approximated as 0.5 × Fblock × delta_free for a linear actuator.
answers.c: The thermal energy absorbed by the active layer.
answers.d: The time derivative of the blocking force.

explanations.a: Incorrect — This describes Newton's Second Law (F = ma).
explanations.b: Correct — Work output is calculated as the area under the force-deflection line, which is 0.5 × Fblock × delta_free.
explanations.c: Incorrect — This represents thermal input, not mechanical work output.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Work is force integrated over distance, not force's time rate of change.

questions.question: Q8. Which of the following material pairs would most likely act as a bilayer actuator under thermal stimulus?

answers.a: Two identical sheets of standard PLA printed with the same raster angle.
answers.b: A layer of high-expansion 4D-Print PLA bonded to a layer of low-expansion Standard PLA.
answers.c: Two layers of PNIPAM hydrogel at uniform temperature.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Identical materials with the same orientation will expand equally, producing zero bending.
explanations.b: Correct — Bonding layers with differing thermal expansion coefficients (CTEs) creates a mismatch that drives bending.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Uniform layers without expansion differences will not bend.
explanations.d: Incorrect — A single isotropic layer will expand uniformly without bending.

questions.question: Q9. How is the curvature (κ) of a bent beam related to its radius of curvature (R)?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Curvature is not the square of the radius.
explanations.b: Correct — Curvature is mathematically defined as the reciprocal of the radius of curvature (1/R).
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is the formula for circumference.

questions.question: Q10. What is a major challenge in bilayer actuators made of two highly dissimilar materials (e.g., hydrogel and PLA)?

answers.a: The materials will blend together and form a single alloy.
answers.b: Interfacial stress can cause delamination (peeling apart) at the boundary.
answers.d: Dissimilar materials cannot be printed in the same lab.

explanations.a: Incorrect — They do not alloy; they are distinct solid phases.
explanations.b: Correct — High differential strain creates severe shear stresses at the interface, which can lead to delamination.
explanations.c: Incorrect — There is no nuclear radiation involved in thermo-mechanical actuation.
